transcript.content: Hi, welcome. What brings you in today?

Hi. Um, I guess what finally made me book the appointment is that I keep dropping the last step on things I really do intend to finish. Like after audits, or after mentoring events at work, I’ll start the follow-up items — I’ll gather my notes, maybe draft the email, open the form, start the review note — and in my head it feels like it’s basically handled. But then a few days later I realize the final email never went out, or the review note is still sitting unfinished, or some form I thought I completed is just… not done.

It’s frustrating because I’m not ignoring it on purpose. I genuinely mean to finish it, and at the time I feel like I’m on top of it. Then I find out later there was this one last piece that somehow didn’t get completed. That pattern is what pushed me to come in.
Did you have similar problems with finishing tasks or missing the last step when you were a child?

Yes, definitely. I mean, I didn’t think of it that way at the time, obviously, but looking back it’s very familiar.

Even in elementary school, my report cards would say things like I was bright or capable, but then there’d always be this other part — like I lost assignments, or I rushed through things and missed small details, or I needed reminders to actually finish the work. And I remember that being frustrating because I could understand the material. It wasn’t that I couldn’t do it. It was more like the paper would vanish, or I’d do most of it and then not turn it in, or I’d think I was done but there was some last little piece I’d skipped.

My mother still jokes about it, actually. She’ll say I could ace a test but forget the project sitting in my backpack. Which is funny now, sort of, but also… that was kind of the pattern. I’d know the information, but the follow-through — getting the assignment where it was supposed to go, remembering the final instruction, finishing neatly — that was where things fell apart.

And I was also the kid who got comments about talking out of turn, needing reminders, that kind of thing. So yes, this “almost finished but not quite” problem feels like it goes way back.
When something ends up unfinished, is it usually because you got stuck checking it or trying to make it feel exactly right?

I don’t think so, no — at least that’s not how it usually feels from the inside.

I mean, I can be careful with things, especially at work, because details matter, but the unfinished thing doesn’t usually come from me sitting there endlessly polishing it or trying to make it perfect. It’s more like… I get it 80 or 90 percent done, and then I shift to the next thing, or I assume I’ll come back to the last part in a minute, and then that last part just sort of drops out of my awareness.

Like if I were stuck checking it, I think I’d remember feeling trapped in it, you know? Instead it’s more that I honestly think I’ve handled it, and then later I find out I didn’t actually send it, or didn’t attach something, or didn’t finish the final note. So no, I wouldn’t describe it as perfectionism exactly. It feels more like the finish line disappears on me.
Do you tend to worry excessively about a lot of different things, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?

I’m not sure I’d describe myself that way, no. I mean, I worry about normal things — work, deadlines, whether I forgot something important, that kind of thing — but I don’t know that I’m sitting around worrying excessively about lots of different areas for no clear reason.

It’s more situational, I think. Like if there’s something I know I might have missed or something hanging over me, then yes, I can get concerned about it. But I don’t feel like I’m constantly worried across the board all the time. At least, that’s not the main thing that made me come in.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days lately?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I have days where I feel discouraged or worn down, especially when I realize I’ve dropped the ball on something or I’m trying to catch up, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling depressed most days.

It’s more like frustration or feeling overwhelmed in the moment, if that makes sense. I can get upset with myself, and then once the immediate problem passes, my mood usually shifts too. So… no, I don’t think “down or depressed most days” really fits.
